North Korea-Linked Hackers Accused of Stealing $6.36 Billion From Binance

A major cryptocurrency security incident has put Binance under international scrutiny after blockchain investigators reported that approximately $6.36 billion was moved from exchange wallets in minutes. North Korea-linked hackers have been blamed for the attack.

By LokkeeVerse · 4 min read

Binance Hit by Massive Cryptocurrency Security Incident

The cryptocurrency industry is facing renewed security concerns following a reported $6.36 billion theft involving wallets belonging to Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.

Blockchain intelligence company TRM Labs reported on October 30, 2026, that approximately $6.36 billion was transferred out of Binance wallets across ten blockchain networks.

According to the company's investigation, most of the funds moved within approximately 20 minutes.

The incident is being described as one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts ever reported.

TRM Labs attributed the attack with high confidence to TraderTraitor, a hacking group linked to North Korea.

However, the investigation is ongoing, and the attribution has not been independently confirmed by a government authority.

How Did the Attack Happen?

According to TRM Labs, the attackers moved funds from Binance-controlled wallets across several blockchain networks.

The affected networks included Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana, XRP Ledger and several others.

Investigators believe the attack involved a compromise of wallet-signing infrastructure.

On Ethereum, the attacker reportedly used a mechanism involving pre-signed authorisations to gain control over the movement of funds.

The transfers happened extremely quickly, making the incident particularly concerning for cryptocurrency security experts.

TRM Labs said preparations had started before the main transfers, suggesting that the attackers had planned the operation rather than carrying out a random attack.

Why Is North Korea Being Linked to the Attack?

TRM Labs attributed the incident to TraderTraitor, a hacking unit associated with North Korea.

The group has previously been linked to major cryptocurrency thefts and attacks against digital asset platforms.

According to TRM Labs, North Korea-linked hackers have stolen approximately $12.8 billion in cryptocurrency across around 100 incidents since 2017.

The firm estimated that approximately $7.4 billion of that amount was stolen during 2026.

These figures highlight the growing role of sophisticated cyber operations in cryptocurrency-related crime.

However, investigators are still tracking the stolen assets and examining how the attackers moved the funds.

Were Binance Customers' Funds Affected?

Following the incident, Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals on several networks as a precaution while investigating the security problem.

The exchange stated that user funds were safe.

That statement will be particularly important to customers because large cryptocurrency security incidents can create uncertainty, trigger withdrawals and affect confidence in digital asset platforms.

The investigation also involved efforts to freeze some of the stolen assets.

TRM Labs reported that stablecoin issuers and the Arbitrum Security Council froze approximately $2.7 billion in assets connected to the incident.

However, some funds reportedly remained beyond the reach of those freezing mechanisms.

What Does the Binance Hack Mean for Cryptocurrency Investors?

The incident is another reminder that cryptocurrency investments carry risks beyond market price movements.

Even when an investor holds a popular digital asset, the platform, wallet infrastructure and security systems used to manage those assets can become targets.

Investors should consider several precautions:

  • Enable two-factor authentication on cryptocurrency accounts.
  • Use strong, unique passwords.
  • Avoid clicking suspicious links or responding to fake support messages.
  • Never share wallet recovery phrases or private keys.
  • Consider secure self-custody options where appropriate.
  • Verify platform announcements through official channels.

It is also important to understand that keeping cryptocurrency on an exchange involves different risks from holding assets in a personally controlled wallet.

The Investigation Continues

The Binance incident could have lasting consequences for cryptocurrency security and the wider digital asset industry.

Investigators are continuing to follow the movement of the stolen funds, while security experts examine how such a large operation was possible.

For Binance, restoring confidence and demonstrating that its infrastructure is secure will be critical.

For the wider cryptocurrency market, the incident reinforces the importance of stronger security systems, international cooperation and faster responses to digital financial crime.
